title: Realization of field-stage operations from completed integral representatives
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type between separated finite-type $k$-schemes. Use the operation datum [def-fix-six-functor-datum] on small pro-etale sites. For every finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\Omega$, put $R_E=\mathcal O_E$ with uniformizer $\varpi_E$. Let $\mathcal I_E(W)=D^b_c(W,R_E)$ be the category of derived-complete complexes over the completed coefficient sheaf whose constructible reductions have cohomology in one finite interval independent of the reduction exponent [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Write $Q_{W,E}:\mathcal I_E(W)\to\mathcal C_E(W)=\mathcal I_E(W)[1/\varpi_E]$ for raw rationalization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], and $\mathcal C_W$ for the common finite-stage category [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients].

Suppose the specified completed pullback, completed tensor, ordinary direct image, compact-support direct image and ambient integral internal Hom preserve these integral categories. For integral inputs $K,L,M$ in their respective source categories, the specified field operations take values in $\mathcal C_E$ and have natural identifications
$$Lf_E^*Q_{Y,E}M\simeq Q_{X,E}Lf_{R_E}^*M,\qquad
Q_{X,E}K\otimes_E^L Q_{X,E}L\simeq Q_{X,E}(K\widehat\otimes_{R_E}^L L),$$
$$Rf_{*,E}Q_{X,E}K\simeq Q_{Y,E}Rf_{*,R_E}K,\qquad
Rf_{!,E}Q_{X,E}K\simeq Q_{Y,E}Rf_{!,R_E}K,$$
$$Q_{X,E}R\mathcal Hom_{R_E}(K,L)\xrightarrow{\sim}
R\mathcal Hom_E(Q_{X,E}K,Q_{X,E}L).$$
Here the internal-Hom arrow carries rationalized integral evaluation to field evaluation, using the displayed completed-tensor identification. These identifications are natural for all localized arrows, not only integral arrows, and compatible with finite coefficient-field extension and the specified scalar associators. On the literal common-stage categories $\mathcal C_W$ the same operations restrict to $\mathcal C$ and are computed by these formulas after moving the inputs to one finite field. Their values, morphisms and evaluations are independent of that field and of the representatives. In particular the common-stage internal Hom is represented by the rational internal Hom at any common finite stage, with its evaluation represented by the same finite-stage evaluation.

proof.text: Put $R=R_E$, $\pi=\varpi_E$ and write $Q$ for the appropriate localization functor. By the preservation hypothesis, each integral operation has its stated integral target. The raw localization has exactly the integral objects, with localized Hom modules [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. For each unary operation $F=Lf_R^*,Rf_{*,R},Rf_{!,R}$, its additive $R$-linear action therefore extends by [lem-pur-semilinear-scalar-localization], with $\phi=\mathrm{id}_R$, to $F_E(u/\pi^r)=Q(Fu)/\pi^r$. These are the specified coefficient-passage operations of [def-fix-six-functor-datum]; for compact support the object formula is explicitly [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. Thus their values lie in the raw target rationalization and give the three unary identifications in the statement. No additional objects or summands have to be adjoined.

proof.text:
Write $B(K,L)=K\widehat\otimes_R^L L$ and $H(K,L)=R\mathcal Hom_R(K,L)$. Both values are integral constructible by hypothesis. The specified rational operations [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] have these object values and on fractions have actions
$$B_E(u/\pi^r,v/\pi^s)=Q(B(u,v))/\pi^{r+s},\qquad H_E(a/\pi^r,b/\pi^s)=Q(H(a,b))/\pi^{r+s},$$
where $a:K'\to K$ is contravariant and $b:L\to L'$ is covariant. Separate $R$-linearity respects the balancing relations in each localized Hom module. If a fraction is changed by a relation $\pi^t(\pi^{r'}u-\pi^ru')=0$, applying either separately linear action gives the same relation in its output Hom module. Hence the formulas are independent of fractions, even with torsion in integral Hom. Functoriality follows from integral functoriality and addition of denominator exponents. The tensor value is exactly $Q(B(K,L))$, giving the displayed tensor identification. This is an application of the explicit defining formulas and the localization relation, not an ambient tensor product with an infinite coefficient field.

proof.text:
The identification of the localized integral internal Hom with the specified rational internal Hom, preserving evaluation, is [lem-coef-rational-operations]. Its hypotheses are precisely these rationalized constructible categories, with completed integral tensor; there is no site-perfectness restriction on the first variable here. Consequently the fifth displayed map is an isomorphism $c:QH(K,L)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_E(QK,QL)$. If $t:QK\otimes_E^LQH(K,L)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(K\widehat\otimes_R^LH(K,L))$ is the tensor identification from step 2, the normalization is the actual equation
$$\operatorname{ev}_E\circ(1\otimes c)=Q(\operatorname{ev}_R)\circ t.$$
The two sides have the same source and target. All these identifications are natural on integral arrows and on localized arrows: a unary naturality square for $u/\pi^r$ is the integral square multiplied by $\pi^{-r}$; a bifunctor square for two fractional arrows is its integral square multiplied by $\pi^{-(r+s)}$. Sums follow by additivity. Thus no faithfulness or torsion-freeness of $Q$ is being used.

proof.text: For finite $E\subset F$ let $\theta^G_{F/E}:T_{F/E}G_E\xrightarrow{\sim}G_FT_{F/E}$ (both inputs extended for a bifunctor $G$) be the following comparisons. For pullback, completed tensor and internal Hom take the specified integral comparisons of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension], the ones whose rationalizations conjugate common-stage arrows in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]; that statement gives naturality, the identity for $F=E$ and compatibility with the composition isomorphisms for $E\subset F\subset F'$. By [lem-zl-specified-hom-scalar-evaluation] the specified Hom comparison is the transpose of scalar-extended evaluation through the tensor scalar map, its identity and tower equalities hold, and both remain true in the raw rationalized categories for arbitrary localized arrows. For $Rf_*$ take the rational comparisons of [lem-sf-strict-direct-image-scalar-comparison], with its identity and tower equation for the associators of [lem-weil-scalar-extension-composition]. For $Rf_!$ take the compact-support coefficient comparisons of [lem-fix-operation-reduction], which commute with rationalization and common-stage scalar extension; the common-stage object comparison is the canonical one of [lem-weil-compact-support-finite-field-independence]. Integral comparisons are rationalized by [lem-pur-semilinear-scalar-localization] for $R_E\to R_F$: the image of $\varpi_E$ is nonzero, hence invertible in $F$, and inverses, composites and the identity/tower equations persist. Thus the Hom comparison identifies extension of evaluation with evaluation after extension, using the tensor comparison.

proof.text:
Use exactly the pairs and morphism colimits of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. A unary $G$ sends $(E,K)$ to $(E,G_EK)$. If $[M,u]:(E,K)\to(F,L)$ is represented at $M$, send it to
$$[M,(\theta^G_{M/F})^{-1}\circ G_M(u)\circ\theta^G_{M/E}].$$
For tensor and internal Hom, place the two objects over their compositum; place the two input arrows over a common field $M$; apply $B_M(u,v)$ or $H_M(a,b)$ and conjugate by the source and target $\theta$ maps. This is the action specified in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Naturality and the tower equation from step 4 say that extending this output to $N\supset M$ gives the same conjugated formula at $N$. Two equal representatives agree at some such $N$, so their images agree there. At one common stage, the middle $\theta$ and its inverse cancel in a composite; the functor laws at that stage then give the common-stage functor laws, also with the first Hom argument reversed. Thus values are constructible at a finite stage, arrows are independent of representatives, and changing the field yields the canonical comparison isomorphism, compatible with further changes.

proof.text:
For inputs over $E$ and $F$, choose $M\supset E,F$. Represent their common-stage Hom by
$$\bigl(M,H_M(T_{M/E}K,T_{M/F}L)\bigr)$$
and represent its evaluation by $\operatorname{ev}_M$ with the source tensor identification. This is an arrow of the literal pair category [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Enlarging $M$ carries this arrow to the same evaluation via $\theta^H$ and $\theta^B$, by the evaluation transpose equation of step 4 [lem-zl-specified-hom-scalar-evaluation] and the tower equations of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension]. Equal arrow representatives give equal evaluation diagrams after common enlargement by step 5. If object representatives are replaced by isomorphic ones, apply the functors of step 5 to those isomorphisms and their inverses; naturality of evaluation in its second variable and its defining dinaturality in the first identify the evaluation arrows under those comparisons. Hence the common-stage operation and its evaluation are represented at any common finite stage and independent in exactly the canonical-isomorphism sense required for objects. This proves the last clauses without replacing the pair category by a Karoubi envelope or an ambient $\Omega$-sheaf category.
